items.question: Under what conditions must this teaching be kept secret in the mortal world?
premises: The teaching must be concealed
Concealment requires deliberate effort
The mortal world contains the lowest of men
items.inference: This teaching should be carefully hidden in the mortal world among unworthy people.
items.plain_english: It must be carefully concealed in the mortal world among the lowest of men.

items.question: To whom may this teaching be transmitted after proper testing?
premises: The teaching may be given
The recipient should be previously accomplished
The recipient must be tested for one year
items.inference: This teaching may be given only to a previously accomplished person tested for one year.
items.plain_english: It should be given to one who is already accomplished and has been tested for one year.

items.question: Which chapter concludes in the text emerged from Candradvīpa?
premises: The text is identified as emerged from Candradvīpa
The section is numbered fifth

items.question: By whose grace has the determination of the Kaula doctrine become known?
premises: The speaker addresses the lord of Kaulas
Knowledge arose by that lord's grace
What is known is the determination of Kaula
items.inference: The speaker has come to know the Kaula determination through the lord's grace.
items.plain_english: O Lord of the Kaulas, by your grace I have come to know the determination of the Kaula doctrine.

items.question: What is the declared identity and essential nature of the individual soul?
premises: The soul is said to be declared
One question asks who that soul is
Another question asks what the soul's nature is
items.inference: The inquiry seeks both the identity and the essential nature of the soul.
items.plain_english: Who is that soul that has been declared, and what is the true nature of the soul?

items.question: Into what does the soul dissolve, and can this whole matter be explained?
premises: The soul is asked about its place of dissolution
The inquiry concerns all these points together
The speaker requests a full explanation
items.inference: The question asks for a complete explanation of where the soul dissolves.
items.plain_english: And into what does it dissolve? Tell me all of that.

items.question: What supreme qualities define the ultimate reality being described here?
premises: The subject is identified as supreme
It is described as partless and eternal
It is described as free from disease and stainless
items.inference: The ultimate reality is characterized as supreme, partless, eternal, and pure.
items.plain_english: He is supreme, partless, eternal, free from disease, and stainless.

items.question: How is the supreme individual soul identified in terms of haṃsa and śakti?
premises: The soul is described as supreme
That same soul is identified as haṃsa
That soul is also identified as the individual of power
items.inference: The supreme soul is identified as haṃsa, the individual associated with power.
uncertainties: The exact doctrinal sense of śakti+pudgalaḥ is context-dependent.
items.plain_english: That soul which is supreme is indeed the haṃsa, the individual embodiment of power.

items.question: Where is the breath-filled vital air said to be situated within living beings?
premises: The subject is the air filled with breath
It is described as situated
Its location is in all living beings
items.inference: The breath-filled vital air abides in all living beings.
uncertainties: Agreement between vāyuḥ and saṃsthitam is irregular in the transmitted form.
items.plain_english: The breath-filled vital air is situated in all living beings.

items.question: What is the soul called immediately upon leaving the physical body?
premises: The condition is merely leaving the body
The subject is then designated by a name
That designation is supreme Śiva
items.inference: Upon leaving the body, the soul is called supreme Śiva.
items.plain_english: As soon as it leaves the body, it is called the supreme Śiva.

items.question: How is this teaching transmitted and received according to traditional lineage?
premises: The teaching is heard in the ear
It comes down through successive tradition
The goddess is addressed as recipient
items.inference: This teaching is received orally through an unbroken traditional lineage.
items.plain_english: O Goddess, it is heard in the ear, having come down through the succession of tradition.

items.question: What effect does merely hearing this knowledge have for the addressed goddess?
premises: The knowledge is described as mere knowledge
It is received by hearing
The fair-faced goddess is addressed
items.inference: Even merely hearing this knowledge is presented as significant for the recipient.
uncertainties: The sentence is syntactically incomplete and continues into the next verse.
items.plain_english: O fair-faced one, by this mere knowledge, heard and received...

items.question: What disciplined practice over six months leads to freedom from bondage?
premises: A practitioner is described as practicing for six months
The practice is associated with the ochre robe
The state aimed at is freedom from bondage
items.inference: One who practices for six months in this renunciant discipline becomes free from bondage.
uncertainties: The syntactic role of kāṣāyaṃ is ambiguous in this compressed verse.
items.plain_english: But whoever practices for six months, in the ochre-robed state free from bondage...

items.question: What result follows for the practitioner freed from all diseases?
premises: The practitioner becomes freed from all diseases
Association with yogis is mentioned
Union or meeting together is indicated
items.inference: Freed from all diseases, the practitioner attains union with yogis.
uncertainties: The exact grammatical construction of saha+melakam is compressed.
items.plain_english: Freed from all diseases, he attains union together with the yogis.

items.question: What teaching about the soul's practice has now been communicated to Bhairavī?
premises: The speaker addresses Bhairavī
Something has been told to her
That content is the practice concerning the soul
items.inference: The teaching on the practice of the soul has been communicated to Bhairavī.
items.plain_english: O Bhairavī, this practice concerning the soul has been told to you.

items.question: To what kind of resolved recipient may this teaching be given?
premises: The teaching is to be given

The recipient has a resolved mind
items.inference: This teaching should be given to a resolved person endowed with all states.
uncertainties: The case mismatch between genitive and locative qualifiers is present in the text.
items.plain_english: It should be given to one who is endowed with all states and has a resolved mind.

items.question: Why must the essential Kaula teaching originating from the yoginīs not be given indiscriminately?
premises: The Kaula essence is identified
Its origin is linked to the yoginīs
Transmission of this essence is prohibited
items.inference: The essential Kaula teaching, originating from the yoginīs, must not be given out.
uncertainties: The syntactic relation of sambhavam to sāraṃ is somewhat compressed.
items.plain_english: The essential Kaula teaching, which has its origin in the yoginīs, must not be given.

items.question: What transformation of the body from ignorance to purity is being claimed now?
premises: The body is now described as pure

items.inference: The speaker claims that her body, once veiled by ignorance, is now pure.
uncertainties: The form deham appears accusative but functions as subject in context.
items.plain_english: Today my body is pure, though it was once struck by the veil of ignorance.

items.question: What auspicious teaching about overcoming time does the speaker now wish to hear?
premises: The speaker expresses a wish to hear
The topic concerns time
The desired teaching is the auspicious deception of time
items.inference: The speaker now wishes to hear the auspicious method for overcoming time.
items.plain_english: Now I wish to hear the auspicious means of overcoming time.

items.question: What assurance is given that death can be destroyed through this teaching?
premises: The speaker promises to explain
There is said to be no doubt
The explanation concerns how death is destroyed
items.inference: The teaching will explain without doubt how death is destroyed.
items.plain_english: I will tell you, without doubt, how death is destroyed.

items.question: How can even a wise person be affected while engaging the nectar's essence?
premises: The context involves the tip of nectar
There is contact with the essence of juice

items.plain_english: Even a wise person may feel a burning sensation at the tip of nectar, through the essence of its juice.

items.question: What yogic technique involving breath at the palate is prescribed for practice?
premises: The practice is located at the root of tongue and palate
The practitioner acts upon the breath
The breath should be drawn in slowly
items.inference: The prescribed technique is to slowly draw in the breath at the root of the tongue and palate.
items.plain_english: Placing attention at the root of the tongue and palate, one should slowly drink in the breath.

The condition is that it has been practiced

items.inference: Practicing this technique for one year destroys old age and death.
items.plain_english: When this is practiced for one year, old age and death are destroyed.

premises: Poison does not enter the body

items.plain_english: Poison does not enter the body, even if one is bitten by great serpents.
